feedback.problem:
Express the Maclaurin series expansion for ${sin}^{2}⁡x,$ given by

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡x={x}^{2}-\frac{{2}^{3}{x}^{4}}{4!}+\frac{{2}^{5}{x}^{6}}{6!}-\frac{{2}^{7}{x}^{8}}{8!}+⋯
$$

using sigma notation.
feedback.worked_solution:
The first four terms of the series are

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & ={x}^{2} \\ {a}_{2} & =-\frac{{2}^{3}{x}^{4}}{4!} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{{2}^{5}{x}^{6}}{6!} \\ {a}_{4} & =-\frac{{2}^{7}{x}^{8}}{8!}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we can express these terms using a common format, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1} & =\frac{(-1)^{1+1}{2}^{2\cdot 1-1}{x}^{2\cdot 1}}{(2\cdot 1)!} \\ {a}_{2} & =\frac{(-1)^{2+1}{2}^{2\cdot 2-1}{x}^{2\cdot 2}}{(2\cdot 2)!} \\ {a}_{3} & =\frac{(-1)^{3+1}{2}^{2\cdot 3-1}{x}^{2\cdot 3}}{(2\cdot 3)!} \\ {a}_{4} & =\frac{(-1)^{4+1}{2}^{2\cdot 4-1}{x}^{2\cdot 4}}{(2\cdot 4)!}.\end{aligned}
$$

We deduce that the general formula for the $n$th term is

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{2}^{2n-1}{x}^{2n}}{(2n)!}\,.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡x & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{2}^{2n-1}{x}^{2n}}{(2n)!}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
